newsitem.title: UK: North Sea to lead 1998 non-OPEC output hike - IEA.
newsitem.headline: North Sea to lead 1998 non-OPEC output hike - IEA.

text.p: The North Sea will lead a surge in oil supply next year from producers outside OPEC, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.

"With added supply of over 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), the North Sea remains the single biggest region in terms of contributions to the total 1998 non-OPEC supply increment of two million bpd," the IEA said in its latest oil market report.
A decline of 470,000 bpd from mature fields will be more than offset by gains of 1.04 million bpd from the start up of 27 new fields and rising output from 25 fields expected on stream in 1997.
Repairs and upgrades to some older fields are also expected to add to next year's North Sea output, the Paris-based agency said.

After revising lower its 1997 estimate of non-OPEC supply growth in recent months by about 400,000 bpd to 1.6 million bpd due to technical problems and weather-related delays, the IEA issued a clear health warning with its 1998 figures.
"The (1998) projection...is predicated on more normal operating conditions than those that occurred in 1996 and the first part of 1997, which constrained supply growth," it said.
Nearly 500,000 of the anticipated growth is expected to come from fields which will have come onstream this year and which will be hitting plateau production levels in 1998.
"The key point of this analysis is that the timing and pace of production increases of the 1997 fields is an important determining factor in the accuracy of the 1998 forecast."
Latin America should add an extra 470,000 bpd to non-OPEC supply next year, bolstered by rapid increases in output from offshore Brazil and central Colombia.
Non-OPEC African producers are expected to add 195,000 bpd with Canada and Australia also lifting output.
The reversal of a 12-year decline in domestic U.S. output due to increasing Gulf of Mexico production and a flattening out of the Russian decline will also boost non-OPEC numbers, the agency said.
